title: id(world_net): manifest_state silently drops a mistyped seed — a present-but-malformed seed reads as the capability-only None and is captured as seed 0

body:
## Problem

`WorldClient::manifest_state` (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:961-995`, on
`origin/main` 075b2de904) reads the two fields of the `world_state`
reply with opposite strictness:

```rust
Some("world_state") => Ok((
    reply["seed"].as_u64(),                                   // :978
    serde_json::from_value(reply["schedules"].clone())
        .context("host sent a malformed schedule map")?,      // :979-980
)),
```

`schedules` is decoded strictly and a malformed map errors. `seed` is
read with a bare `as_u64()`: a **present but mistyped** seed — `"42"`,
`-1`, `1.5`, `{}` — silently becomes `None`, indistinguishable from
the one legitimate `None` case, a capability-only read where the host
deliberately hides the seed (#240; `world_session/tests.rs:685`
"schedule_and_world_state_frames_round_trip_and_hide_the_seed").

## Verified this run (laptop probe, real `id` crate, scripted host)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-policy-wt/pkgs/id/tests/probe_policy_reply.rs`,
test `probe_manifest_state_seed_shapes`:

- CONTROL `{"type":"world_state","seed":42,"schedules":{"a":1}}` →
  `Ok((Some(42), {"a":1}))`.
- CONTROL no `seed` field (capability-only shape) → `Ok((None, {}))`
  — the legitimate `None`.
- CASES seed `"42"` / `-1` / `1.5` / `{}` → all `Ok((None, {}))`,
  identical to the legitimate hidden-seed result.
- ORACLE mistyped `schedules` (`{"a":"x"}`) → `Err`, proving the
  sibling field in the same reply is validated.

## Why it matters

The consumer is world-manifest capture
(`commands/world.rs:1145`, `capture_world_state`): it takes the
returned seed into `WorldState { seed: seed.unwrap_or(0), .. }`, the
state that `id world apply`/diff reconciles against. An admin read
whose seed arrived mistyped is silently downgraded to the
capability-only shape and then baked in as **seed 0** — a fabricated
install seed in the captured manifest, with no error anywhere. The
reply's own contract already distinguishes the two cases (field absent
= hidden; field present = the seed); the client just has to check
presence before type, the way the schedules arm checks its type.

## Acceptance criteria

- `manifest_state` errors when the `seed` field is present but not a
  `u64` (string, negative, float, object, array, bool), with an error
  naming the malformed seed; a genuinely absent seed still returns
  `None` for capability-only reads.
- Regression tests with a scripted host covering: numeric seed,
  absent seed, and each mistyped-seed shape; mistyped `schedules`
  continues to error.
- No change to the host side or to the #240 seed-hiding behavior.
